desc1: Beyond the Horizon is a student enterprise dedicated to creating personal growth. Through active discussions and independent explorations in various areas of development, students can engage with themselves & with each other on innovative ideas.
desc2: We often hold weekly meetings where one member prepares a Google Slides presentation to share with others about their current interest relating to ideas of self-growth. This allows a balanced observation of various aspects of development, rather than committing to only one.
desc3: There is no other organisation within this school which promotes learning in the long-term, which would benefit students after they leave school. We prepare for our members to be ready for their future, whatever that may be.

desc1: The Cubing Enterprise is dedicated to fostering problem-solving, spatial reasoning, and creative thinking through speedcubing. Our initiative brings together students of all skill levels to master various puzzles, from classic 3x3 Rubik's cubes to complex non-standard variants. We actively enrich school life by organizing exciting Junior School house competitions, building school spirit, and encouraging friendly rivalry. Beyond competitive solving, we explore the artistic and engineering aspects of cubing by designing creative mosaic art and custom structures using puzzle blocks. Ultimately, our enterprise aims to build an inclusive community centered on the cube.
desc2: Our meetings are usually for lessons, as we have beginner to advanced level cubers that we teach. On special occasions, we will bring in creative activites to endorse in, making cubing much more fun and engaging. Sometimes, we will hold inner competitions between us to measure our ability in the subject. We have a tradition of hosting and organizing internal house competitions(mainly in the junior school) for cubing, and we will be hosting it this year as well.
desc3: Our Cubing Enterprise stands out by blending logic, competition, and visual art into a unique hands-on platform. While many wonderful enterprises focus on valuable community service and traditional projects, we offer a complementary space dedicated to cognitive skill-building and creative design. We go beyond teaching speedcubing algorithms by using cubes as an artistic medium, constructing large-scale mosaics and original structures that transform abstract problem-solving into tangible art. By organizing energetic Junior School house competitions, we also bridge age groups and build vibrant school spirit, providing a fresh way for students to challenge their minds, collaborate, and express their creativity.

desc1: Our enterprise explores not only music itself, but also the business and industry surrounding it, including industry trends, marketing strategies, and patterns of consumer behavior. Throughout the term, each member will select an album of their choice, write an in-depth review, and have their work published on our official website. For students who are interested in music, business, marketing, or cultural and consumer trends, we hope this enterprise will provide them with a unique opportunity to develop analytical and writing skills while engaging with music from a broader perspective.
desc2: Throughout the term, each member will select an album of their choice, write an in-depth review, and have their work published on our official website. (offrecord.international)
desc3: What makes our enterprise unique is that we approach music from beyond a merely artistic perspective. By combining music criticism with marketing, consumer analysis, and cultural / political influences, members explore how the music industry operates and how cultural trends influence both artists and audiences. Rather than simply discussing whether an album is ‘good’ or ‘bad,’ we intend to examine the wider context, including, promotion, external influences, and industry trends. Each member of the enterprise also produces an in-depth album review covering most of these aspects, which is then published on our official website, giving students the opportunity to develop their own critical voice while creating a tangible piece of published work.

desc1: The Life Below Water Enterprise is a student-led initiative focused on protecting marine ecosystems and promoting sustainable relationships between people and the ocean. Founded at NLCS Jeju, the enterprise explores issues including blue carbon and the blue economy, plastic pollution and coastal sustainability. Its purpose is to not only raise but also turn awareness of ocean-related issues into practical action by developing campaigns and engaging with wider environmental initiatives.
desc2: LBW Enterprise combines environmental education, campaigns and practical projects. Members research marine and coastal issues and communicate what they learn through the website lbwenterprise.com. We have organised initiatives such as postcard relays and educational materials to encourage people to think about their relationship with the ocean. The enterprise also explores blue carbon and the blue economy, and we consider how marine ecosystems can support both environmental protection and sustainable development. Beyond school activities, LBW Enterprise has participated in wider initiatives, including the 2025 UNEP–COBSEA Sea of Solutions, where an eight-student Korean delegation took part in the Youths session.
desc3: What makes LBW Enterprise special is that we use multiple approaches with regards to a particular environmental issue: blue carbon and the blue economy. Members can contribute in multiple ways including joining the Olle Trail Clean-up Bryant, joining our research team and innovating publicity/awareness methods.

desc1: Tides of Care is a student-led initiative and a non-profit organisation dedicated to countering the growing voices of violence and war, and standing alongside their victims, including refugees and individuals suffering from the mental and social aftereffects of conflict. We believe that empathy and informed action can change how communities respond to displacement. Through awareness campaigns, fundraising, seminars, and other creative initiatives, we amplify the voices of refugees, challenge discrimination, and promote peace, inclusion, and understanding. By working with refugee-led organisations and encouraging our school community to engage with these issues, we aim to turn our efforts into meaningful, lasting support.
desc2: Tides of Care aims to raise awareness about the challenges faced by refugees in terms of environmental justice, access to education, mental health, and cultural inclusion. We are planning to engage in this issue by establishing platforms to raise awareness, organising fundraising drives, hosting educational programs, addressing challenges through creative writing/art activities, and more. By focusing on these interconnected issues, we hope to inspire a more inclusive and empathetic school community that is actively engaged in making a difference both locally and globally.
desc3: What makes Tides of Care special is that we do not just provide passive support, but communicate and connect our school community directly with the people we advocate for. On 19 November 2025, we hosted a ‘Dialogue with Refugees’ session, where we invited refugee speakers living in Korea to share their experiences firsthand, and held a fundraising initiative for their organisation, Migration to Asia Peace. In December 2025, our Christmas bazaar sold cookies, candles, and scented wax made by refugees from Good Samaritan House, supporting their livelihoods. As a student-led initiative, we combine advocacy, fundraising, and creativity to show that we, as students, can make a lasting difference.

desc1: We are an interscholastic service enterprise that works with student artists with learning disabilities to produce collaborative art and organise exhibitions. We collaborate with social welfare centres in Jeju (탐라장애인종합복지관) as well as various convention centres to act as art galleries.
desc2: Each year, members receive a selection of artworks created by student artists with autism. Members are expected to contribute with a piece of art or poetry, or musical performance reacting to their selected work. The two pieces of art will then be exhibited side to side in a yearly gallery exhibition, which the members will be expected to attend.
desc3: We create real impact. Having been founded 4 years ago, ABST has delivered on its final goal each year, providing a space where both NLCS students and artists with autism can express their creativity and overcome prejudice through collaboration.

desc1: Eco Legal Person Supporters is an enterprise dedicated to advocating the Rights of Nature movement. We promote the eco-legal personhood (legal recognition of non-human natural entities as subjects bearing rights) while developing a deep environmental stewardship among students and the local community. Through developing a connection with legal innovations with regional ecology, our aim is to shift people's perspectives of nature: shifting from viewing the ecosystem as a source of disposable resource to respecting it as a vital entity. Ultimately, we advocate for the rights of animals, oceans and delicate habitats to exist and thrive.
desc2: We publish research-driven articles on our website, highlighting critical regional environmental topics such as Jeju's unique marine ecosystems and other ecological events. On foot, we also conduct coastal cleanup sessions along the shores of Jeju, removing trash and plastic waste to protect marine life directly.
desc3: Taking approaches that bridge high-level legal advocacy with tangible and localized actions. Although eco-legal personhood is frequently discussed politically and academically, we bring this concept directly into the students and local communities through accessible digital storytelling and direct cleanup initiatives. Furthermore, by expanding our writing beyond marine life to include other terrestrial ecological events, we offer a holistic view on environmental rights. We actively protect our oceans while giving a voice to nature through student journalism.

desc1: Maths and Arts Enterprise is a student-led group that explores the connection between mathematics and artistic creativity. Our purpose is to show that mathematics is not limited to equations and calculations, but can also be used to understand, design and create visual art. By bringing together mathematical ideas and artistic expression, we aim to make mathematics more accessible and engaging while encouraging students to approach familiar concepts from new perspectives. The enterprise also provides opportunities for students with different interests and strengths to collaborate, combining logical thinking with creativity to produce meaningful work.
desc2: Our activities focus on creating art inspired by mathematical ideas and exploring the mathematics behind visual patterns and designs. Students investigate concepts such as geometry, symmetry, proportion, tessellation, sequences and mathematical patterns before applying them to creative projects. Activities may include designing mathematical artwork, producing physical or digital pieces, developing products, and preparing displays or workshops for the wider school community. Through these projects, members experience the complete creative process: developing an idea, considering its mathematical basis, designing and refining the work, and presenting the finished product to others.
desc3: What makes Maths and Arts Enterprise special is that it brings together two subjects that are often treated as opposites. Mathematics provides structure, patterns and logical relationships, while art allows those ideas to be interpreted creatively and visually. Rather than simply studying either subject, members use one to explore the other. This makes the enterprise accessible to students with different strengths: someone interested in mathematics can experiment with creativity, while someone interested in art can discover the mathematical ideas underlying their work. Most importantly, our projects turn abstract mathematical concepts into something that can be seen, created and shared.

desc1: Our enterprise aims to further the learning of and incorporation of digital archivist efforts within our own school. By cultivating both the technical skills and the historical awareness necessary for such work, we hope to foster a culture of stewardship—where the past is not merely remembered, but actively protected and shared through the powerful tools of the present.
desc2: 1. Volunteer online for digital transcriptions and archive tagging every Friday, with the Smithsonian  2. Hopefully host a school-wide transcribe-a-thon!
desc3: Digital archives and transcriptions should not be considered mere replicas, but rather a guard against the loss of primary historical accounts, sources, and documents that are otherwise subject to natural erosion and decay. By digitising these sources, we ensure that delicate manuscripts, oral histories, and ephemera—so often subject to decay, disaster, or neglect—are not only saved but in fact made accessible to generations far removed from their creation. In doing so, we democratise history, allowing students, scholars, and curious minds alike to engage with the past in a format both enduring and dynamic.

desc1: Youth Rights Activists Enterprise aims to raise awareness of youth rights and empower young people to create meaningful change in their communities. We aim to ensure that young people recognise that their voices matter and have the capacity to make a difference. Through collaboration with national organisations and collaborative projects, we, as adolescents ourselves, explore issues that directly affect us and provide opportunities for students to turn their understanding into action.
desc2: A key activity of the Youth Rights Activists Enterprise is the annual LENS project, conducted in collaboration with the Korea Council of Children’s Organizations. Under an annual theme, the group chooses its focus on a particular issue affecting young people and investigates them from a youth-rights perspective. Students gather the views and experiences of other young people through research and survey, analyses the results, and extends to offering possible solutions. The activity aims to grow awareness of youth rights issues in the community and create a meaningful change.
desc3: We are the one and only NLCS Jeju's Human Rights enterprise. We connect with external organisations such as Korean council of children’s organisation to actively advocate for children and teenager's rights. Through campaigns, discussions, research and community projects, we explore issues ranging from education to equality. Our main goal is to turn student's ideas and concerns to tangible action.

desc1: ABO Supporters is a student-led service society that aims to raise awareness about blood donation and its importance in supporting patients who rely on donated blood. We hope to encourage a culture of volunteering and community support within our school by helping students understand how blood donation can make a meaningful difference. Through awareness campaigns, or enrichment week activities, we share accessible information about blood donation and encourage people to learn more about how they can contribute when they are eligible. Our goal is not simply to recruit donors, but to build a more informed and caring school community.
desc2: ABO Supporters carries out a range of awareness and service activities throughout the school year. These include creating posters and social media content about blood donation, organising campaigns around events such as World Blood Donor Day, and sharing information about why blood donation matters. We support blood donation events by helping promote them within the school and doing our duties on the day that the bus comes. We also explore ways to support patients, including creating certificates and messages for children receiving cancer treatment.
desc3: What makes ABO Supporters special is that we focus on making an important but sometimes unfamiliar topic accessible to students. Rather than simply telling people to donate blood, we focus on education, awareness and creating a positive culture around volunteering. We use creative methods such as posters, social media, art and collaborations with other school communities to communicate our message. We are also a student-led society, meaning that our members can bring their own ideas and take an active role in developing projects. Most importantly, we hope to show that even small actions, such as learning about blood donation or sharing accurate information, can contribute to helping others.

desc1: SNHS aims to enhance the school community's engagement with scientific research and provide opportunities for students to expand the scope of their academic exploration into science.
desc2: SNHS aims to run a range of activities for encouraging scientific research and exploration, including publishing journals and hosting in-school science fairs.
desc3: SNHS provides unique opportunities to try exploring the sciences beyond individual work or a set curriculum by allowing students to interact actively with the school community.
